title: Timing Load Breakdown
objective: Add opt-in execution timing breakdowns for observed module, addon, and native-kernel initialization without distorting statement timing

oracles: deterministic timing clock and REPL/kernel integration tests

handoff.summary: Adds display-only `%time --breakdown` and Sage `time --breakdown` parsing, typed nested initialization spans for Python modules, native addons, runtime modules, and first-load native kernels, compact aggregate-only default output, explicit inclusion in wall time, Node CPU reporting, browser wall-only formatting, CLI help, documentation, and deterministic host/kernel/compiler tests.
risks: The integration receipt has five unrelated baseline failures: one superseded exact-matrix serialization counter and four stale FFI ratchets expecting three libraries and 190 declarations before M4RI. The current integration branch has already refreshed those ratchets and passes them.
Initialization spans are synchronous by design; future asynchronous lazy loaders need an async-aware span primitive before they can appear in the tree.
next_steps: Integrate onto the current dense-qq-resources branch and run the refreshed integration suite.
Use the typed native-kernel spans in the separate cold-production-kernel performance ratchet.
